per_item.question: 2 (buildability of pass 1)
per_item.spec_says: step 1 builds the policy file and reader from section ORC-POL
per_item.should_say: resolve, or hand step 1 a decision procedure for, the seven items below
per_item.finding: A competent worker cannot build pass 1 from section 2 without guessing seven times. (a) DIAL VS WORD: ORC-POL-3 asserts a per-model 0-9 dial; section 12.3 makes dial-vs-categorical an open design choice; step 1 is the first BUILD step, so the parser's value domain is undecided at build time. (b) RESERVED: ORC-POL-6 is normative that 'the parser accepts exactly 0-9 plus a reserved sentinel; anything else is a parse error', while section 12.2 defers the sentinel's spelling as moot with no live consumer — the parser must accept a token whose encoding is deliberately unchosen. (c) FAMILY VOCABULARY: the worked file's caps use claude/fable/deepseek/ollama-cloud/local — 'fable' is the keeper's spelling (tools/fleet-keeper.sh:325) and 'ollama-cloud' is managent's (src/managent/main.zig:347), so the example is a third vocabulary that matches neither reader, and the pane renders a sixth set (claude, deepseek, ollama-cloud, local, ox-alpha, plus claude-fable). ORC-POL-1 says one file for all readers but never says whose family names the file uses. (d) MISSING ENTRY: the worked file has no ox-alpha cap and the pane renders its cap as a dash; a missing cap therefore means 'uncapped', which is precisely the unstated default ORC-POL-1 says cannot survive ('env vars never invent a default the file does not state'). ORC-POL-6 fixes this for appetite ('an unknown model resolves to a refusal') and says nothing for caps. (e) NAMED CONDITIONS: expiry values 'next-ollama-quota-refresh' and 'blind-test-reveal' are 'resolved by the arbiter' (ORC-POL-2), but the arbiter is step 2 and the reader is step 1, and no source of truth for either condition exists; nothing says whether an unresolvable condition fails open or closed. (f) ONE FACT, TWO DOORS: the ollama quota is encoded twice in the worked file — appetite dial 0 keyed by short name ('glm') and allow_deny.deny keyed by canonical label ('glm-5.2') — with no precedence rule, inside the artifact whose reason for existing is the census finding that a second door is where data is lost. (g) PARSE FAILURE SCOPE: 'refused at parse time' is not said to be entry-level or file-level, and dispatch's behaviour on a refused file (fail open or fail closed) is unstated, though the house precedent is fail-closed (tools/fleet-keeper.sh:399-408, unreadable dir means cooldown).
per_item.how_verified: read section 2 and section 12 line by line; extracted both live appetite tables (tools/fleet-keeper.sh:325-326 DEFAULT_APPETITE, src/managent/main.zig:347-357 family_appetite at d79726c) and compared their key sets to the worked file's and the worked pane's
per_item.would_refute: a design doc already resolving these — but ORC-PLAN-1 places design AFTER spec ratification, and section 12 explicitly leaves (a) and (b) open
per_item.severity_reason: medium rather than major: none of the seven is a wrong statement, they are absences, and the sprint's own audit loop would surface them at design; (b) is closest to major because the two statements are in direct contradiction
